title: BiggerPockets Alternatives for Tax-First Investors (2026)
metaDescription: BiggerPockets alternatives for investors who want tax-first planning, STR coaching, or a CPA who works with landlords. Who each fits, and when to stay put.
h1: BiggerPockets alternatives for investors who want tax strategy, not only deal talk
summary: For investors who have outgrown forum answers and want tax-first planning, STR coaching, or a CPA who works with landlords.
verdict: BiggerPockets is the best free starting point in real estate, and for finding, analysing, and talking through deals it is still hard to beat. If that is what you need, stay. The people who go looking for an alternative usually need something the platform was never built to give them: a tax plan for their specific return, a coach who answers their questions the same day, or a CPA who actually works with landlords.

Match the alternative to the gap. A real-estate-focused CPA firm fixes the filing and planning gap. Short-term rental coaching fixes the execution gap for one property model. [Legacy Wealth Blueprint](/legacy-wealth-blueprint) fits the person who wants tax strategy, debt, accounts, and protection handled as one written plan, with property as one piece of it rather than the whole point. We publish this page and offer that program, so read our section with that in mind.

competitorProfile.what: BiggerPockets is an online community for real estate investors that has been around since 2004. It is best known for its forums, its podcasts, its books, and its deal calculators. The free tier is large; a paid Pro membership adds calculator limits, market data, landlord tools, and other extras, and the company also sells bootcamps and books through its own publishing arm.
competitorProfile.format: Self-serve. You read, listen, post questions, and run numbers. Nobody on the platform knows your return, your W-2, or your entity structure unless you post the details, and forum replies are opinions from other investors, not advice from someone accountable to you.
knownFor: Forums where thousands of active investors answer questions on every strategy from house hacking to syndications
The BiggerPockets Real Estate Podcast and Real Estate Rookie, both free and published several times a week
Calculators for rental analysis, BRRRR, fix-and-flip, and similar deal maths
Books on rental investing, BRRRR, and real estate tax basics
Bootcamps, meetups, and directories for finding agents, lenders, and tax professionals
bestFor: Beginners who need to understand the models before spending anything
Investors who want to sanity-check a deal or a market with people who have done it
Anyone who learns well from long-form podcasts and reading
Finding local professionals and investor-friendly agents through the directories
notIdealFor: A specific tax plan for your own return, entity, and income mix
Accountability: nobody follows up if you stop showing up
Short-term rental setup where you want a coach reviewing your listing, pricing, and lease
People who already know the strategy and need implementation help, not more information

whyPeopleLook: They have listened to hundreds of episodes and still have not bought a property. Information is not the bottleneck any more; execution is.

They have a high W-2 income and want to know whether the [short-term rental loophole](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole), [cost segregation](/tax-strategies/cost-segregation), or [real estate professional status](/tax-strategies/real-estate-professional-status) applies to them, and forum threads give five different answers.
Their current CPA is a generalist who has never filed a cost segregation study or asked about material participation hours.
They want one person to answer questions about their deal, not a thread that goes quiet after two replies.
They own one or two rentals and realise the tax plan, the debt plan, and the retirement accounts were never coordinated.
They are drawn to short-term rentals specifically and want a program built around that model rather than general rental content.

alternatives.name: Legacy Wealth Blueprint
alternatives.bestFor: W-2 earners and business owners who want tax strategy, debt, accounts, and protection in one written plan, with real estate as one of the pillars rather than the whole program.
strengths: A custom 12-month Wealth Strategy Snapshot built from your numbers, plus an optional review of your prior-year return in the first weeks to find what was missed
Weekly live coaching calls with replays, a 1-on-1 Legacy Wealth Guide with bi-weekly check-ins, and a private community for 12 months
A CPA Implementation Brief near filing season that you hand to your own CPA, so the strategies actually make it onto the return
Real estate is taught step by step inside the Investment Vehicles pillar, alongside retirement accounts and the tax rules that decide whether a rental helps your return
Access to a partner network (tax strategist, estate attorney, credit advisor, entity setup)
tradeoffs: It is not a deal-finding program. You will not get a market list, a deal pipeline, or an agent referral network the way you do on BiggerPockets
Nobody files your return or contacts your CPA for you; you carry the brief to them
Preston Seo is a personal finance educator, not a CPA or an attorney; licensed advice comes from the partner network or your own professionals
Built for people earning roughly six figures and up who want to optimise what they already earn; a beginner with a small income is better served by free content first

alternatives.name: A real-estate-focused CPA firm (WCG CPAs & Advisors, The Real Estate CPA)
alternatives.bestFor: Investors who already own property and want the return prepared and the planning done by people who work with landlords every day.
strengths: They file. That is the one thing no course, community, or coaching program on this list does

Firms like WCG publish long, detailed public guides on S corporations and rental taxation, and Hall CPA (The Real Estate CPA) publishes heavily on REPS, the short-term rental rules, and cost segregation, so you can judge their thinking before you call
They see hundreds of investor returns a year, which means fewer conversations where you explain what a cost segregation study is
Planning and preparation sit under one roof, so the strategy and the filing do not drift apart
tradeoffs: Most firms have minimums and waitlists, and planning is usually a separate engagement from preparation
You get advice on the tax questions you bring, not a coach who checks whether you followed through on debt, accounts, or protection
Firm capacity is finite; response times during filing season are slower than a coaching program
Verify current services, licensure, and scope directly; firms change their intake rules often

alternatives.name: Tax Alchemy (Karlton Dennis)
alternatives.bestFor: Investors and business owners who want a firm to build and implement the tax plan, including entity work and cost segregation, and are comfortable being quoted on a call.
strengths: Done-for-you scope: advisory, entity structuring, implementation help, real estate tax planning, cost segregation, and 1031 exchange work are all listed on its site

tradeoffs: It is a tax firm, not a real estate community; deal analysis and market research are on you
The founder's public bio describes him as a tax strategist without listing a CPA or EA licence; ask which person on the team holds the licence and in which state
Cost segregation and bonus depreciation move tax from later to now; ask any firm to walk through the exit and recapture, not only year one

alternatives.name: Short-term rental coaching (Airbnb Ascension)
alternatives.bestFor: Someone who wants cash flow from one short-term rental alongside their job and wants a coach on the setup rather than a forum.
strengths: Airbnb Ascension assigns a dedicated 1-on-1 STR coach for onboarding, day-to-day questions, and deal reviews, plus weekly live calls and a private operator community

tradeoffs: It teaches rental arbitrage, meaning you lease the property and sublet it as a short-term rental. Because you do not own the building, there is no depreciation and no [STR loophole](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole) benefit from an arbitrage unit
If the tax benefit is the goal, you need to own the property; Legacy Investing Show runs a separate done-for-you STR acquisition service for that case, discussed on the strategy call
You do the market research and the landlord calls yourself, with scripts and roleplay; it is coaching, not a hands-off service

scenariosIntro: These are the situations that come up most often on our strategy calls when someone mentions BiggerPockets. The pick is a starting point, not a verdict on your facts.

scenarios.situation: High W-2 earner, no rentals yet, wondering whether the STR loophole is real
scenarios.pick: Free content first, then Legacy Wealth Blueprint or a real estate CPA
scenarios.why: Read the [STR loophole guide](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole) and [REPS vs STR](/tax-strategies/reps-vs-str-loophole) before spending anything. Once you know the hours test and the ownership requirement, decide whether you want a plan across your whole return (Blueprint) or a firm to model one purchase (CPA).

scenarios.situation: Two or three long-term rentals, generalist CPA, never heard of cost segregation from them
scenarios.why: This is a filing and planning gap. A firm that does investor returns all day will find what a generalist misses, and they can run the [cost segregation](/tax-strategies/cost-segregation) maths with your actual numbers.

scenarios.situation: Still analysing deals after two years of podcasts
scenarios.pick: Stay on BiggerPockets, add a local REIA, set a deadline
scenarios.why: More paid education will not fix an execution problem. Post a real deal for feedback, meet lenders in person, and give yourself a date. BiggerPockets is genuinely the right tool here.

scenarios.situation: Wants cash flow from one Airbnb alongside a job, does not want to buy yet
scenarios.why: Arbitrage is a cash-flow model, not a tax model. A coach who reviews the lease, the listing, and the pricing is worth more than general rental content for this specific job.

scenarios.situation: Owns one rental, has a 401(k), credit card debt, and no idea how the pieces fit
scenarios.why: The problem is coordination, not property knowledge. One written plan that sequences the debt, the accounts, and the tax moves, with a guide checking in, is what the program is built for.

whereLisFits: Legacy Wealth Blueprint is built for people earning roughly six figures and up who want to optimise the income they already have. Tax is the first pillar, and it covers entity structures, deductions, tax-advantaged accounts, and the W-2 and business strategies most investors never hear from a generalist CPA. Real estate is taught step by step as one of the investment vehicles, next to retirement accounts, so the decision to buy a rental happens inside a plan instead of on its own.

What you get is specific: lifetime access to the 100+ video curriculum, 12 months of weekly live coaching calls with replays, a custom 12-month Wealth Strategy Snapshot, an optional Prior Year Tax Return Diagnostic in the first weeks, a 1-on-1 Legacy Wealth Guide with bi-weekly check-ins, an AI advisor trained on the system, and a CPA Implementation Brief before filing season. [Stephanie Dailey](/blog/stephanie-dailey-legacy-wealth-blueprint-case-study), a software engineer with household W-2 income, saved over twenty thousand dollars in taxes in her first year by her own count. [Albert](/blog/albert-legacy-wealth-blueprint-case-study), an ER physician in California, put his net worth growth at 25 percent and cut his home insurance in half. Both are individual, self-reported results, not a promise.

On third-party review sites, Legacy Investing Show holds a 4.2 TrustScore from 66 Trustpilot reviews, with 77 percent five-star and 9 percent one-star. Read both ends on the [reviews page](/reviews) before you decide.
whereLisDoesNotFit: It does not fit if what you want is a deal pipeline, market data, or a community of people trading off-market leads. BiggerPockets and a local REIA do that job better and cheaper. It does not fit if you want your return filed; the program produces a brief for your CPA and nobody on the team contacts your CPA directly. It does not fit if you are early in your career with a modest income and no debt problem to solve, because the strategies need enough income to move real money.

It also does not fit someone who wants an STR-only program. The Blueprint teaches real estate as one pillar; if you want a coach on one short-term rental, that is Airbnb Ascension, and if you want an owned STR acquired and set up for you, that is a separate service discussed on the strategy call.
howToDecide: Write down the one thing BiggerPockets is not giving you. If the answer is deal flow or feedback, you do not need an alternative; you need to post a real deal and set a deadline.

Check whether the tax strategies you are excited about actually apply to you. The [STR loophole](/tax-strategies/short-term-rental-loophole) needs ownership and material participation. [REPS](/tax-strategies/real-estate-professional-status) needs 750 hours and more than half your working time. Read the guides and be honest about your hours.
Decide whether you want knowledge, labour, or a plan. Knowledge is free content and courses. Labour is a CPA firm. A plan with someone checking in is coaching.
Ask every paid option the same four questions: who answers me, do you file, what is delivered in writing, and what happens when the term ends. Get the answers in an email.

Run the numbers first. Use the [cost segregation calculator](/tools/cost-segregation-savings) and the [STR break-even tool](/tools/str-break-even-occupancy) so you walk into any call knowing what a property would actually do for your return.

faqs.q: Is BiggerPockets worth it, or should I pay for a program?
faqs.a: For learning the models and getting feedback on deals, BiggerPockets is worth it and mostly free. Pay for a program only when you can name the gap: a tax plan for your return, a coach for one property model, or a CPA who works with investors. If you cannot name the gap, the problem is execution, and no program fixes that.

faqs.q: What is the best BiggerPockets alternative for tax strategy?
faqs.a: For filing and return-specific planning, a real-estate-focused CPA firm. For a written plan that coordinates tax with debt, accounts, and protection, with a guide checking in, Legacy Wealth Blueprint. For a firm to implement entity work and cost segregation, Tax Alchemy is one of the names people compare. None of these replaces the other; they solve different problems.

faqs.q: Does Legacy Wealth Blueprint teach how to find and analyse deals?
faqs.a: It teaches real estate step by step inside the Investment Vehicles pillar, including how a rental interacts with your tax return, but it is not a deal-finding program. For underwriting practice and market data, BiggerPockets calculators and forums are the better tool.

faqs.q: Can I use the short-term rental loophole with an Airbnb arbitrage unit?
faqs.a: No. The STR loophole depends on depreciation, and depreciation requires ownership. An arbitrage unit is leased, so it produces business income and expenses but not depreciation. Arbitrage is a cash-flow strategy; owning an STR is where the tax strategy lives.

faqs.q: Should I get a real estate CPA or a coaching program first?
faqs.a: If you already own property, get the CPA first so the current return is right. If you own nothing yet and the question is what to do with your income, a plan comes first and the CPA implements it. Many people end up with both: the program sets the strategy, the CPA files it.

faqs.q: How is Legacy Wealth Blueprint different from a BiggerPockets Pro membership?
faqs.a: Pro adds tools, data, and access on a self-serve platform. Blueprint adds people: weekly live coaching, a 1-on-1 guide with bi-weekly check-ins, a written 12-month plan, and a partner network. One is a better toolbox; the other is a coached plan. Pricing for the Blueprint is not published and is discussed on the strategy call.

keyLine: Stay on BiggerPockets for deals and community. Look elsewhere only when you can name the gap: a tax plan for your return, a coach for one property, or a CPA who works with landlords.

title: Tax Alchemy Alternatives: 10 Options Compared (2026)
metaDescription: Tax Alchemy alternatives for owners and investors: Legacy Wealth Blueprint, Tax Strategy Accelerator, WealthAbility, Mark J. Kohler, Anderson, fee-only planner.
h1: Tax Alchemy alternatives: ten options, who fits each, and when Karlton Dennis is the right call
summary: Ten options for people who priced a done-for-you tax firm and want to know what else exists, from memberships and coached plans to fee-only planners and doing it yourself.
verdict: Tax Alchemy is a done-for-you tax planning firm. If you want a team to build the plan, set up the entities, run the cost segregation, and prepare the return, and you are comfortable being quoted on a call, it is a legitimate way to hand the whole job off. Most people searching for an alternative are not rejecting the firm; they are discovering that they wanted something cheaper, more educational, more licensed, or more focused on the W-2 side of their life.

Sort by what you want to hand off. Want the labour done: compare Tax Alchemy with Tax Goddess, a fee-only planner, and a firm like AE Tax, and ask each who holds the licence. Want to learn first: Tax Strategy Accelerator from the same founder, or a fixed-scope course. Want ongoing answers for a multi-entity setup: Anderson Platinum. Want a licensed CPA and attorney teaching: Mark J. Kohler. Want a vetted advisor matched to you: WealthAbility. Want to learn and be coached through a written plan that covers more than tax: [Legacy Wealth Blueprint](/legacy-wealth-blueprint). We publish this page and offer the Blueprint, and our earlier three-way comparison, [Karlton Dennis vs Mark Kohler vs Legacy Wealth Blueprint](/blog/karlton-dennis-vs-mark-kohler-vs-legacy-wealth-blueprint), reaches the same conclusions.

competitorProfile.what: Two things share the Karlton Dennis name, and people mix them up. Tax Alchemy is the firm: its site lists Karlton Dennis as CEO and describes tax strategy analysis, entity structuring, implementation help, real estate tax planning, cost segregation, and 1031 exchange work, with tax preparation offered to advisory clients. Tax Strategy Accelerator is the education membership from the same founder: video courses, a private community, recordings of weekly client calls, and AMA sessions with tax advisors. Karlton Dennis built the audience on YouTube, and his public bio describes him as a tax strategist without listing a CPA or EA licence; Tax Alchemy describes its team as licensed tax strategists.
competitorProfile.format: The firm is a 1-to-1 advisory engagement quoted on a call. The membership is self-paced video plus community and call recordings. Neither publishes a fixed scope for every client, so ask exactly what is included before you sign.

A lower-commitment education membership for people who want to learn first

Self-starters who want a large video library and community through the membership
notIdealFor: W-2 earners with no business and no property; no firm can invent deductions you do not have
People who want the person on the sales call to be the person who does the work

whereLisFits: Legacy Wealth Blueprint is built for people earning roughly six figures and up who want to optimise what they already earn, whether that income is a salary, a business, or both. Where Kohler's membership answers owner questions on a schedule, the Blueprint delivers a plan: a custom 12-month Wealth Strategy Snapshot, an optional Prior Year Tax Return Diagnostic in the first weeks, and a CPA Implementation Brief around months ten to eleven that you hand to your own CPA. The team does not contact your CPA; you keep them.

The support model is the other difference. A 1-on-1 Legacy Wealth Guide runs your onboarding and checks in every two weeks, weekly live coaching calls come with replays, the Wealth Circle community and the AI advisor cover the questions in between, and a partner network with a tax strategist, estate attorney, credit advisor, and entity setup partner handles the licensed work. Lifetime access to the 100+ video curriculum covers five pillars: tax optimisation, debt and credit leverage, income diversification, investment vehicles including real estate and retirement accounts, and protection. [Albert](/blog/albert-legacy-wealth-blueprint-case-study), an ER physician in California, put his net worth growth at 25 percent and cut his home insurance in half; [Abigail](/blog/abigail-legacy-wealth-blueprint-case-study) calculated just under a hundred thousand dollars in first-year return by her own maths. Individual, self-reported results, not typical and not a promise. Third-party reviews: a 4.2 TrustScore from 66 Trustpilot reviews, 77 percent five-star, 9 percent one-star, on the [reviews page](/reviews).
whereLisDoesNotFit: If you want a licensed CPA and attorney teaching you directly, Kohler is the better fit and we will not pretend otherwise. If you want legal documents drafted, a trust set up, or a self-directed IRA custodied, his firms do that and we do not. If you are an established owner with a complex multi-entity structure, his depth on that topic is greater. The Blueprint also does not file returns, does not publish pricing, and is not built for someone early in their career with a modest income or someone who would pay from an emergency fund.
howToDecide: Name your income type. Mostly W-2: pick something that covers W-2 strategies first. Mostly business: Kohler's owner focus or a firm goes deeper on entity work.

Decide whether you want answers or a plan. A membership with live Q&A answers the questions you bring. A written 12-month plan with a guide tells you the order of operations and checks that you did it.

Decide how you feel about buying services from the educator. It is convenient and it is a conflict; both are true. If you want independence, hire a local CPA and attorney and use the books as your syllabus.

Check the specific strategies against your facts before any call: the [S-corp strategy](/tax-strategies/s-corp-strategy), the [Solo 401(k)](/tax-strategies/solo-401k), and [S-corp vs the QBI deduction](/compare/s-corp-vs-qbi-deduction) are the three that decide most owner questions.
Ask every option who answers you, whether anyone files, what is delivered in writing, and what happens when the term ends. Get it in an email.

faqs.q: Is Mark J. Kohler a CPA or an attorney?
faqs.a: Both. His KKOS Lawyers profile lists him as a licensed attorney in Utah and Idaho and a licensed CPA in California, Utah, and Idaho. He is a senior partner at that firm.

faqs.q: What is the trifecta structure?
faqs.a: Kohler's framework for owners: an operating entity such as an LLC or S-corp on one side, a holding entity for assets like rentals on the other, and a revocable living trust above both, with your personal return in the middle. It is a way of organising operations, assets, and estate planning; whether you need all three pieces depends on what you own.

faqs.q: What is the best Mark J. Kohler alternative for a W-2 earner?
faqs.a: Legacy Wealth Blueprint, because it covers W-2 strategies, tax-advantaged accounts, debt, and protection in one plan rather than assuming an entity. If you own nothing yet, start free: max the retirement accounts and the HSA, then decide whether a business or a property is next.

faqs.q: Does Legacy Wealth Blueprint set up entities or trusts?
faqs.a: No. It teaches when an entity makes sense and includes an entity setup partner and an estate attorney in its partner network, but the legal work is done by those professionals or your own. KKOS Lawyers does that work inside Kohler's ecosystem, which is a real advantage if that is your main need.

faqs.q: Should I just read Kohler's books and hire a local CPA?
faqs.a: For a simple structure, yes, that is often enough. Read the books, run the S-corp and Solo 401(k) guides against your numbers, and hire a CPA who plans rather than only prepares. Buy a program when you need accountability, a written plan, or a licensed teacher on a schedule.

faqs.q: How does Business Owner HQ compare with Legacy Wealth Blueprint on support?
faqs.a: Business Owner HQ lists biweekly live masterminds with Kohler, a forum, an app, and an AI assistant. Legacy Wealth Blueprint lists weekly live coaching calls, a 1-on-1 guide with bi-weekly check-ins, a private community, an AI advisor, and a written 12-month plan. One is group access to a licensed expert; the other is a coached plan with a dedicated point of contact. Pricing for the Blueprint is discussed on the strategy call, not published.
